guides.intro: SGit Vaults keeps photos, videos and large files in an encrypted vault that a teammate can open. A vault you create is kept on this device and needs no account, no access key and no network until you share it.

callouts.text: A shared vault: on the server, and you can add and change.

Create a vault, on this device.

callouts.text: Paste the vault key, read key or link you were sent.
A read key can only look. To add files to a shared vault you also need an access key for the server, which is not part of the vault key: ask whoever sent it.
Your own name for the vault, on this device.

guides.intro: A vault holds folders and files, like a folder on a computer, with every change kept as a signed commit.

guides.title: SGit Vaults: share a vault, and create one on the server
guides.pictures: SGit Vaults: iPhone, light, from sgit-app-screens.yml run 19 on dev (commit e62bf68, 14 November 2026).
guides.intro: Sharing gives somebody the vault's key. Whoever holds it can read everything in the vault, including its history, and it cannot be taken back: give it to people, not to places.

callouts.text: Send the way in: a message with the key, a link for a browser and the steps for the person receiving it. Send it only by a channel you trust.
What a key can do, said before you see it.
The vault key: read and write.
The read key: read only.
A name, for you. The key is made here and kept on this device only.
Share it: put it on the server at once. Off, it stays on this device until you share it.
The access key the server needs to take a new vault, kept in the Keychain.
